{{Quote|The Gand known as Zuckuss is clearly schizophrenic and exhibits multiple personality disorder.|[[Gawynn Karastee]]|<ref name="EGAS" />}}
'''Schizophrenia''' was a severe mental illness that was often characterized by delusions and [[Hallucination/Legends|hallucinations]]. Sufferers would sometimes demonstrate a proclivity to violent behavior. This condition could affect multiple [[Species/Legends|species]], such as [[Aleena/Legends|Aleena]], [[Gand/Legends|Gands]], and [[Human/Legends|Humans]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Eh, my friend? What's that? Oh, yes. He stinks of Sith, all right. But what's he doing here now? Haven't I suffered enough?|[[Kazdan Paratus]] speaking to his junk mannequin of [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="The Force Unleashed (novel)">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref>}}
Schizophrenia was a mental illness that would afflict its sufferers with delusions and [[Hallucination/Legends|hallucinations]]. These hallucinations were often auditory and would manifest as voices.<ref name="UA">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref> Some schizophrenics would have visual hallucinations, as exemplified by the [[Aleena/Legends|Aleena]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Kazdan Paratus]], who believed that his junk constructs of the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] were actual living individuals.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

Schizophrenics would sometimes exhibit violent behavior. [[Victor Jun]], an [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] recruiter, would often act on the orders given to him by the voices in his head, which sometimes involved murder.<ref name="UA" /> [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], a [[Gand/Legends|Gand]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], also suffered from schizophrenia,<ref name="EGAS" /> which developed after he had left his [[Gand (planet)/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="OSAVC8">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 8|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 8]]</ref> Co-morbid with his [[multiple personality disorder]], the condition caused him to hear voices<ref name="TMA">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref> and it contributed to the Gand's violent outbursts.<ref name="FF61">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 61|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 61]]</ref> It was speculated by [[Gawynn Karastee]], the forensic [[psychiatrist]] who diagnosed Zuckuss, that the Gand's mental illnesses may have stemmed from his role as a [[Findsman/Legends|findsman]].<ref name="EGAS" />

Although most common with living sentients, droids and other machines are also capable of possessing schizophrenia. The [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], for instance, often had schizophrenic arguments with itself, as a side-effect of its owners modifying the ship's computer to utilize three different models of [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]].<ref name="MFOWM">''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Schizophrenia, as a disorder, first appeared in [[2001]], with the publication of [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]. In a journal entry attributed to Gawynn Karastee, the mental illness served as a [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] to explain the drastic personality changes in Zuckuss, most notably in his appearance in ''[[The Bounty Hunter Wars]]'' series and the previously-established [[canon]] of ''[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]''. The disorder appeared again in the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]] supplemental ''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]'', with the introduction of the character Victor Jun.

Due to its derivation from [[Wikipedia:Greek language|Greek]] for ''"split-mind,"'' schizophrenia, in media, is sometimes depicted similarly to [[Wikipedia:dissociative identity disorder|dissociative identity disorder]].<ref name="OWH">{{BookCite|author=Tracy Knight|title="More Simply Human." On Writing Horror.|publisher=Writer's Digest Books|date=2007|pages=147}}</ref><ref name="Schizophrenia">{{WebCite|url=https://www.psychiatry.org/patients-families/schizophrenia|text=Schizophrenia|work=Schizophrenia|archivedate=20190904071424}}</ref> For example, in both the ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 61]]'' and the [[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 8|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 8]], the characteristics of Zuckuss's schizophrenic diagnosis were described as being more akin to multiple personality disorder, with the illness being termed as simply "schizophrenia". However, real-world schizophrenia is characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech patterns, abnormal psychomotor behavior, and a negative or flat affect,<ref name="DSMV">{{WebCite|url=http://www.dsm5.org/ProposedRevision/Pages/proposedrevision.aspx?rid=411|text=APA DSM-5|work=Schizophrenia, proposed revision|archivedate=20110601021710}}</ref><ref name="Schizophrenia" /> which are not present in a diagnosis of multiple personality disorder.<ref name="DSMV-DID">{{WebCite|url=http://www.dsm5.org/ProposedRevision/Pages/proposedrevision.aspx?rid=57|text=APA DSM-5|work=Dissociative Identity Disorder, proposed revision|archivedate=20110530081352}}</ref><ref name="MayoClinic">{{WebCite|url=http://www.mayoclinic.com/health/dissociative-disorders/DS00574/DSECTION=symptoms|text=Dissociative disorders: Symptoms|work=Dissociative disorders|archivedate=20080622074646}}</ref>
